title: Take-over confirm renders the referee's name twice
evidence:
+      html.p([class("text-sm text-slate leading-relaxed")], [
+        html.text(copy.refcheck_take_over_confirm_body(name)),
+      ]),
+      html.p([class("text-xs text-slate")], [
+        html.text(name),
+      ]),

pub fn refcheck_take_over_confirm_body(name name: String) -> String {
  "Automated messages stop, and "
  <> name
  <> "'s details + the attempt log are yours. If they complete the form anyway, it still shows up here."
}
detail:
The confirm body already interpolates the referee's name; the extra bare-name

renders it a second time. Looks like a leftover placeholder for the §7.7 chips.
recommended_fix: Delete the redundant name line, or render the referee's contact chips there if the §7.7 wireframe intended them inside the confirm.

title: Menu 'Substitute referee' clobbers an open edit-trio's typed values
evidence:
+        RefcheckSubstitute -> #(
+          Model(
+            ..menu_closed,
+            refcheck_edit: Some(prefill_refcheck_edit(
+              model,
+              call_id,
+              RefcheckEditSubstitute,
+            )),
+          ),
+          effect.none(),
+        )

+    Unreachable ->
+      list.append(
+        case call.hooks.can_take_over {
+          True -> [RefcheckTakeOver]
+          False -> []
+        },
+        case call.hooks.can_substitute_referee {
+          True -> [RefcheckSubstitute]
+          False -> []
+        },
+      )
detail: On an Unreachable row the substitute affordance exists in both the overflow menu and the row body; choosing the menu entry while the trio is open unconditionally rebuilds the edit state from the row's snapshot, discarding typed input.
recommended_fix: In UserChoseRefcheckAction, keep an existing edit for the same call/kind instead of prefilling, or hide the menu substitute entry while the trio is open.

title: B3 'never re-derives' invariant holds only for take-over/substitute
detail: Start/skip/re-enable entries are still derived from call.status alone; only take-over/substitute consult the hooks, so the claimed invariant is false for three of five entries.
recommended_fix: Gate start/skip/re-enable on server hooks too, or narrow the comment so the documented invariant matches the code.

title: start_check's whole-application start (slot: None) is unreachable
evidence:
+/// POST .../reference-checks/start?slot=<slot> — RC4.3 per-row start (the
+/// RC2.3 endpoint with the pre-declared slot variant). `slot: None` is the
+/// whole-application start.
...
+  let url = case slot {
+    Some(s) -> url <> "?slot=" <> s
+    None -> url
+  }

                  reference_checks_api.start_check(
                    vid,
                    aid,
                    Some(slot),
                    csrf,
                    on_response,
                  )
detail: Every client call site passes Some(slot); the None branch and its doc line describe a whole-application start nothing invokes. Dead capability, misleading doc.
recommended_fix: Drop the None branch and the whole-application doc line, or wire the call site if the RC2.3 endpoint still needs it.

title: Action names are free strings with a silent substituted-toast fallback
evidence:
+              let toast_copy = case action {
+                "start" -> copy.refcheck_toast_started
+                "skip" -> copy.refcheck_toast_skipped
+                "re-enable" -> copy.refcheck_toast_re_enabled
+                "take-over" -> copy.refcheck_toast_taken_over
+                "correct" -> copy.refcheck_toast_corrected
+                _ -> copy.refcheck_toast_substituted
+              }
detail: The action string is duplicated at each fire site and matched here; the catch-all means a mistyped name silently toasts 'Referee substituted' instead of failing loudly.
recommended_fix: Carry the RefcheckAction/RefcheckEditKind constructor on ApiReturnedRefcheckAction instead of a string, or assert on unknown names in debug.

title: W8 late-response guard keys on payload presence, not navigation
evidence:
+    ApiReturnedRefcheckAction(call_id, action, result) ->
+      // r1 (W8): the late-response guard the fire helpers' comments promise —
+      // a stale answer after the landlord navigated away is dropped (the
+      // inflight marker is keyed by call id and cleared by the route reset).
+      case find_refcheck_call(model, call_id) {
+        None -> #(
+          Model(
+            ..model,
+            refcheck_action_inflight: set.delete(
+              model.refcheck_action_inflight,
+              call_id,
+            ),
+          ),
+          effect.none(),
+        )
+        Some(_) ->
detail: The drop decision is find_refcheck_call on application_detail, not route: if the payload survives navigation (not cleared in this diff), a late response still toasts and refetches. The documented guarantee only holds when navigation clears application_detail.
recommended_fix: Also consult route/inflight state (cleared by the route reset) in the guard, or clear application_detail on navigation so the promise matches the code.

title: Cancel on the always-open correction trio resets values but never closes
evidence:
+fn view_correction_surface(
+  call: ReferenceCallDetail,
+  app: Application,
+  slot: String,
+  edit: Option(RefcheckEdit),
+) -> Element(Msg) {
...
+      view_edit_trio(call, slot, edit, RefcheckEditCorrect),

+      html.button(
+        [
+          attribute("data-testid", "refcheck-edit-cancel-" <> slot),
+          attribute("type", "button"),
+          event.on_click(msg.UserCancelledRefcheckEdit(call.reference_call_id)),
...
+        [html.text("Cancel")],
+      ),

+    UserCancelledRefcheckEdit(_call_id) -> #(
+      Model(..model, refcheck_edit: None),
+      effect.none(),
+    )
detail: The awaiting-correction trio renders unconditionally, so Cancel only clears edit state — the form stays visible with values re-prefilled from the row. A cancel that visibly cancels nothing.
recommended_fix: Drop the Cancel button from the correction surface, or give it a collapsed state that hides the trio.
